query: How do review facets differ by sentiment label?

per_column.name: quality_defect_presence
per_column.rationale: Interpretable, well-separated categories (defect types vs not_present). This is an external facet that can be cross-tabulated against sentiment to reveal that negative reviews concentrate defect mentions.

per_column.name: expectation_gap_type
per_column.rationale: Clear, meaningful categories describing types of unmet expectation. Well-distributed and groupable, enabling comparison of how expectation gaps differ across sentiment labels.

per_column.name: explicit_recommendation
per_column.rationale: Ordinal, interpretable stance scale (advise_against to strongly_recommend). Highly associated with sentiment but remains a distinct facet with good category separation, ideal for segmentation. Some restatement risk since recommendation tracks sentiment closely, but it is a genuinely different variable.

per_column.name: usage_fit_audience
per_column.rationale: Interpretable categories describing fit for intended use/audience. Well-separated and groupable, allowing exploration of how usage-fit framing differs by sentiment.

judge.rationale: All four columns are external, associational facets with interpretable, well-separated categorical scales that can be grouped and cross-tabulated against label_pos. None merely restate the focus verbatim, though explicit_recommendation is strongly correlated with sentiment and edges toward redundancy. Distributions are balanced enough (not near-constant) to support meaningful comparison. As a set they directly serve the query 'how do review facets differ by sentiment label,' realising the EDA claim well.
